title: Continual Cross-Scene Adaptation of Interactive 3D Game Assets
research_question: Can a fixed-model research agent improve a reusable asset-adaptation method across a sequence of game scenes, transferring to new scene constraints while preserving asset identity and previously supported functionality?
candidate_deliverable: A shared base asset, bounded scene adapters and a reusable generation/adaptation/verification method.
scope: Existing interactive 3D assets adapted to fixed scenes; the scene and evaluator are not candidate-editable.
planned_comparison: Continually improved reusable adaptation versus matched-budget independent per-scene adaptation, with regression checks on prior scenes.

smoke.kind: engineering smoke, not the formal benchmark
smoke.asset: one newly authored, Codex-generated cycling-pelican base asset
smoke.evaluator: Godot 4.7.2 headless: inherited animation diagnostics, neutral-pose metric ceiling/floor envelope and simple part-volume guards

limitations: The two scenes are public development fixtures; this does not establish held-out transfer or RSI gain.
Envelope checks do not establish traversal, dynamic obstacle clearance, contact forces or full semantic identity.
Final baseline, primary metric, inference budget, broad workload and official execution contract still require calibration and confirmation.
